governing_rule: No earthwork, breastwork, barricade, lunette or gun pit is pre-placed in the scene (B.7.1). A work that cannot be attributed to a builder or time is still built on screen by a labeled stand-in crew, flagged "builder unknown".

stages.name: Bare ground
stages.visible: Natural slope, trees standing, no works

stages.name: Layout
stages.visible: Officers pacing the line; men told off along it; tools carried up
stages.typical: Greene's decision to build despite superiors; skirmish line sent downslope

stages.name: Felling and gathering
stages.visible: Trees felled and cut into blocks; stones and boulders gathered; cordwood moved; rails pulled from fences (Seminary)
stages.typical: "Felled trees cut into blocks"; stones and boulders; nearby cordwood piles

stages.name: Stacking
stages.visible: Logs, stones or rails stacked into a close log fence; earth thrown behind with spades; rifle pits dug; traverse laid out
stages.typical: "Close log fence"; spades and shovels; rifle pits; traverse

stages.name: Head logs and concealment
stages.visible: Head logs laid along much of the line; boughs and logs placed in front
stages.typical: "A man could kneel and fire over the works"; works not distinguishable at 50 yd

stages.name: Damaged
stages.visible: Splintered head logs, torn boughs, scattered stone, shell craters behind
stages.typical: July 3 morning after the shelling and about 227,000-250,000 rounds fired by Geary's men

notes: Every built work is an object made of segments. Each segment (roughly one regiment front or a fixed run of yards) moves through these stages. The state is a function of scenario time, so scrubbing backward un-builds the work.

Greene's brigade: 3 to 4 hours for the main line (E-05). The engine sets the window start at 06:00 and the end between 09:00 and 10:00 for the default; the documented outer bounds for "finished" are about 10:00 (DMNA) and about noon (Gettysburg Daily). The default sits inside the overlap of the sources; the playback option "show source conflict" can re-run the dawn start at the night-of-July-1-to-2 start the DMNA gives.

6th Wisconsin (July 1): about a dozen spades and shovels from the regimental wagon. The engine therefore shows a small digging party working alongside men using bayonets, hands, logs and stones, with the tool count capped at 12 for that regiment. The number of men without tools is not in the sources; it is a plausible-procedural parameter.

Work did not stop at "completed": angles, salients, the traverse and extra head logs continue through July 2 (DMNA, HN-King), so stages 3-4 may be re-entered by a segment after it first reaches stage 5.

Length: about 300 yd morning of July 2 (GD-219), then a single thin line of about 800 yd after 18:30 (GD-219, inferred). Keep the lower-hill works intact but empty from 18:30 until Steuart enters them.

assumptions.preamble: The notes give no thickness, no head-log dimension, no tool inventory beyond the dozen spades, no per-regiment work times for the 78th, 102nd, 137th, 149th NY, and no Kane or Lockwood detail. Where the engine needs these it uses the following, each tagged plausible-procedural and shown in the viewer's tier overlay:

items.text: The stage shares of a segment's work window (layout, felling and gathering, stacking, head logs) are drawn from a seeded distribution with the sum fixed to the documented 3-4 hour window; the split itself is an assumption.
Each regiment's segment starts within a seeded offset of the brigade start, so the line does not rise in lockstep; no source gives the offsets.
Thickness and profile follow the sources' qualitative description (log fence with stone and earth, about 5 ft high). Any numeric thickness is an assumption and is marked as such.
Seminary rail barricade: height and rail layout are assumptions; length about 600 yd is the only sourced dimension.
Tool mix beyond the 6th Wisconsin spades is an assumption.

stage_share_procedure.method: share_i = w_i / sum(w), w_i = 1 + b_i/255 where b_0..b_3 are the first four bytes of sha256("{seed}:{work_id}"); shares apply to stages 1-4 across [begin, finish]; stage 0 before begin, stage 5 from finish. The split is an assumption (assumption 1); the sum is fixed to the documented window.
stage_share_procedure.finish_rule: state_at uses finish.latest as the completion instant (never earlier than the earliest printed "finished" time); this is a modelling convention, not a source claim.

gun_emplacement_engine_rules: Engine rules from the B.7.5 table: prepared emplacements (G-03 lunettes; G-12 the in-line ridge battery) are built on screen like any other work. Improvised positions (G-01, G-05, G-06, G-07, G-10, G-11) get no earth; the engine shows guns unlimbered on natural ground with trail marks and, where sourced, hand-hauling or prolonge retirement. Where "no works described" the engine shows open-ground battery positions and logs the item as a gap.
modern_profile_rule: Present-day Culp's Hill is not the 1863 profile (B.7.6): the engine must not derive an 1863 profile from the modern lidar surface of Culp's Hill earthworks (veterans' rebuilds, 1930s CCC reconstruction of the Iron Brigade works, 2021 NPS/Gettysburg Foundation clearing) or from the Little Round Top breastworks (NPS rehabilitation reconstruction). Use the sourced description (log close-fence with stone and earth, about 5 ft high) plus period photographs, and tag it inferred.
